items.summary: An open-source, self-hosted Slack alternative (AGPL-3.0): agents are full workspace members with a role, a budget, and a computer and browser of their own, working on schedules or events, while merges, deploys and anything sensitive wait for your approval in the chat. One command installs it on your own Tailscale network with private HTTPS, and phone apps connect straight to it. Launched November 9, with 1,590 stars in its first week.
items.title: agentes.chat: Open-source self-hosted team chat where people and AI agents work in the same channel (launched Nov 9, AGPL-3.0)

items.summary: n8n Labs' open-source personal agent (Apache 2.0, research preview): it runs on your Mac, Windows PC or own server, inside a private local VM with its own browser, finishing multi-step jobs across Gmail, Calendar, Slack, Notion and the web, and asks before it sends, pays or deletes anything. Bring your own model, including a local one, and drive it from Telegram or WhatsApp. Released November 10.
items.title: Nod: n8n Labs' open-source personal agent with a computer and browser of its own (released Nov 10, Apache 2.0)

items.summary: An open-source personal agent that runs entirely on your own machine, with no token fees for local inference: its PolyStrata engine keeps a MoE model's busiest experts on the GPU and the rest in RAM or on SSD, so the 125B Qwen3.8-Flash-Next runs on a 12 GB card. A proactive 'Another Me' watches your inbox and calendar, speaks up only when it matters, and files mail and meetings into a personal wiki every night for all agents to share. Mac tiers are covered too. Launched November 10.
items.title: Linger: A fully local open-source personal agent that fits a 125B model on a 12 GB GPU (launched Nov 10)
